browserMethod.scope: Completed standalone pages 01 through 12 only; excludes Computer and separate wallet-provider harness.
browserMethod.harness: Isolated headless Chrome, fresh browser context per page, reduced motion, initial viewport 1440x1000, later 390x844 resize.
limitations: Route interception disables the browser HTTP cache. This is an instrumented audit session, not a repeat-visit cache benchmark or typical-user traffic sample.
Non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests are deliberately blocked. Home third-party POST failures are harness effects.
Paint timings are browser PerformancePaintTiming entries from initial desktop navigation; resizing does not provide independent mobile navigation paint measurements.
Snapshot elapsedMs and page dwell are not application load latency and are not reported as such.
Resource sizes are browser ResourceTiming observations, not a packet capture, host bandwidth measurement, or blanket wire budget. Encoded and decoded body sizes are distinct.

Resource totals deduplicate entries repeated across snapshots by navigation ID, URL, initiator type and start time. They cover observed entries through the last snapshot, excluding the separately reported navigation document and potentially later API responses.

Top-frame ResourceTiming does not enumerate all child-frame subresources; cross-origin timing restrictions or other browser behavior can yield zero byte fields. Zero byte fields do not prove no transfer.

Long tasks are deduplicated by navigation ID, start and duration. Counts include the recorded dwell and interactions; pages have unequal dwell. No task attribution, controlled runtime benchmark, LCP, CLS, or INP claim is made.
No outer document/body overflow at sampled widths does not establish that every inner component avoids clipping or overflow.

API HTTP errors, JavaScript page exceptions, request failures and DevTools response-body capture errors are separate categories. Successful 200 responses with inspector eviction are not reclassified as application failures.
